questions.prompt: Which word is closest in meaning to COPIOUS?
questions.explanation: Copious describes something present in large amounts; abundant preserves that meaning, while the other choices concern strength, certainty, or distance.

questions.prompt: A RECEPTIVE listener is most likely to be:

choices.C: determined to preserve every opinion unchanged

questions.explanation: Receptive describes willingness to receive and consider suggestions or information; it does not imply interruption, deafness, or resistance to change.

questions.prompt: An ABSTRUSE explanation is:
questions.explanation: Abstruse means difficult to comprehend, usually because of complexity or obscurity; neither brevity, humor, nor numerical content defines it.

questions.prompt: Which word is most nearly opposite in meaning to WISTFUL?
questions.explanation: Wistful suggests a gently sad longing for something absent; contented instead describes satisfaction with what one has.

questions.prompt: Which word is most nearly opposite in meaning to SCRUPULOUS?
questions.explanation: Scrupulous can describe careful attention to correctness and ethical standards; careless reverses that attention rather than reinforcing it.

questions.prompt: A material described as IMPERVIOUS to water is the opposite of a material that is:
questions.explanation: Impervious material does not let water pass through; permeable material does, making permeability the relevant opposite.

questions.prompt: A screw thread changes turning motion into forward movement. Which device makes the most similar change?

choices.A: A mirror that sends light back toward its source
choices.B: A sleeve that protects a folded map
choices.C: A rack-and-pinion mechanism that moves a straight toothed bar when its gear turns
choices.D: A whistle that makes a sound when air passes through it

questions.correctAnswer: A rack-and-pinion mechanism that moves a straight toothed bar when its gear turns
questions.explanation: Both mechanisms convert rotation into straight movement; the alternatives reflect light, protect an object, or convert airflow into sound.

questions.prompt: An anagram changes the order of letters while retaining every letter and its number of occurrences. Which action has the same relationship to its original material?

choices.A: Shuffling a deck changes card order without adding or removing cards.
choices.B: Sharpening a pencil removes some wood.
choices.C: Mixing paints produces a new combined color.
choices.D: Enlarging a photograph changes its dimensions.

questions.correctAnswer: Shuffling a deck changes card order without adding or removing cards.
questions.explanation: An anagram and a shuffle rearrange the same individual elements without changing their identities or quantities; the alternatives remove, combine, or resize material.

questions.prompt: A stencil can reproduce a letter without containing any ink. Which comparison has the same relationship between a guide and the material needed to make its product?

choices.A: A candle contains the wax that it burns.
choices.B: A cookie cutter defines a shape but supplies none of the dough.
choices.C: A reservoir stores the water it releases.
choices.D: A packet holds the seeds that are planted.

questions.correctAnswer: A cookie cutter defines a shape but supplies none of the dough.
questions.explanation: The stencil and cutter constrain a product’s shape without supplying its material; the alternatives contain the substance they use or release.

questions.prompt: Which word shares the idea of TWO found in BILINGUAL, BIPEDAL, and BILATERAL?
questions.explanation: Bicolored means having two colors; its bi- carries the same two meaning, unlike the coincidental initial letters in the alternatives.

questions.prompt: HEAD of a committee, HEART of a city, and FOOT of a mountain use body-part words figuratively. Which phrase belongs in that group?
questions.explanation: Backbone figuratively names the argument’s essential supporting structure; the other phrases identify actual anatomical parts of people.

questions.prompt: Which group contains ONLY terms for a deliberately unfinished state?
questions.explanation: A draft, sketch, and rough cut can each be a preliminary version awaiting development; the alternatives include final outcomes or spatial terms.

questions.prompt: A notice says: "This entrance is closed to deliveries, except flowers for the stage." A bouquet is being delivered for the stage. What does the notice establish?

choices.A: Every other entrance must be locked.
choices.B: All flowers anywhere may use this entrance.
choices.C: The bouquet’s carrier must be an actor.
choices.D: The bouquet is exempt from this delivery restriction.

questions.correctAnswer: The bouquet is exempt from this delivery restriction.
questions.explanation: The stated exception covers flowers intended for the stage; it does not establish access elsewhere or the carrier’s occupation.

questions.prompt: A catalog lists a novel under its original title and again under its translated title. Both entries explicitly refer to the SAME work. What follows?

choices.A: Two catalog entries need not represent two different works.
choices.B: Every translated title has a different author.
choices.D: A work can never have more than one title.

questions.correctAnswer: Two catalog entries need not represent two different works.
questions.explanation: The entries are different descriptions of one identified work, so counting entries alone would overcount distinct works in this case.

questions.prompt: Every word on a card is either printed in black or printed in red. Every red word is underlined. At least one word is NOT underlined. What must be true?

choices.A: Every black word lacks an underline.
choices.B: There are more black words than red words.
choices.C: No word is printed in red.
choices.D: At least one word is printed in black.

questions.correctAnswer: At least one word is printed in black.
questions.explanation: A word without an underline cannot be red under the rule; since black and red exhaust the possibilities, that word must be black.

questions.prompt: To WIELD a tool is to:
questions.explanation: Wield means hold and use something, especially a tool or weapon; concealing, repairing, and exchanging do not express that action.

questions.prompt: To WINNOW a long list of proposals is to:
questions.explanation: Winnow means separate out unwanted material; applied to proposals, it describes narrowing the list by removing less suitable candidates.

questions.prompt: A GENTEEL manner is most nearly:
questions.explanation: Genteel describes polished manners and social refinement; the alternatives instead suggest haste, distrust, or forceful demands.

questions.prompt: ARABLE land is suitable for growing crops. Which description is most nearly opposite?
questions.explanation: Arable concerns suitability for cultivation; land unfit for cultivation reverses that meaning, while the alternatives preserve it.

questions.prompt: A CONTENTIOUS participant often starts arguments. Which description is most nearly opposite?
questions.explanation: Contentious means inclined to argue or quarrel; an agreeable, cooperative participant displays the opposite approach to disagreement.

questions.prompt: In describing a writing style, FLORID most nearly contrasts with:
questions.explanation: Florid style is elaborately ornamented; plain, restrained language removes that ornamentation rather than adding more of it.

questions.prompt: Condensation changes water vapor into liquid. Which process completes the reverse transformation?

choices.A: Freezing changes liquid water into ice.
choices.B: Grinding breaks a solid into smaller pieces.
choices.C: Filtering removes particles from a liquid.
choices.D: Evaporation changes liquid water into vapor.

questions.correctAnswer: Evaporation changes liquid water into vapor.
questions.explanation: Evaporation reverses the vapor-to-liquid change by taking liquid water back to vapor; the alternatives perform different transformations.

questions.prompt: A confluence is a place where streams join into one flow. Which location has the most similar relationship to what meets there?

choices.A: A summit above the surrounding valleys
choices.D: A junction where separate traffic routes merge

questions.correctAnswer: A junction where separate traffic routes merge
questions.explanation: Both a confluence and the described junction are meeting points where separate paths combine; height, storage, and overlooking are different relationships.

questions.prompt: A pun can present the SAME expression with two possible meanings. Which visual device has the most similar structure?

choices.A: An enlargement that makes every feature bigger
choices.B: A border that covers a damaged edge
choices.C: An ambiguous drawing that can be seen as either a vase or two faces
choices.D: A copy that removes all identifying marks

questions.correctAnswer: An ambiguous drawing that can be seen as either a vase or two faces
questions.explanation: The pun and ambiguous drawing preserve the same presented form while allowing different interpretations; the alternatives change size, cover damage, or remove information.

questions.prompt: Which word belongs with NEVER, SELDOM, and OFTEN because it describes how frequently something happens?
questions.explanation: Always describes frequency, like never, seldom, and often; nearby, abroad, and backward instead indicate place or direction.

questions.prompt: RENT, LEASE, and LEND can describe temporary use without transfer of ownership. Which action instead transfers ownership to a purchaser?
questions.explanation: Selling transfers ownership to the buyer; hiring, borrowing, and renting concern use or possession without that purchase-based transfer.

questions.prompt: Which group contains ONLY verbs that can describe repeated back-and-forth movement?
questions.explanation: Oscillate, shuttle, and seesaw all describe movement between positions in alternating directions; the other groups include one-way changes or remaining still.

questions.prompt: A notice says visitors MAY request a guided tour. It gives no other rule about tours. What does MAY establish here?

choices.A: Visitors have permission to request a tour.
choices.B: Every visitor must request a tour.
choices.C: Every requested tour must be free.
choices.D: Tours are forbidden unless visitors arrive together.

questions.correctAnswer: Visitors have permission to request a tour.
questions.explanation: May grants permission; it does not create an obligation, establish a price, or add a condition about arriving together.

questions.prompt: A sealed envelope contains an accurate prediction, but nobody can verify WHEN the prediction was written. Which claim remains unproved?

choices.B: The prediction agrees with the event.
choices.C: The prediction was written before the predicted event.
choices.D: The writing date has not been verified.

questions.correctAnswer: The prediction was written before the predicted event.
questions.explanation: Accuracy concerns agreement with the event; without evidence of the writing date, it does not establish that the statement preceded the event.

questions.prompt: Every accepted form is either inspected or signed, but NOT both. Every signed form is sealed. An accepted form is NOT sealed. What must be true?

choices.B: It was signed but not inspected.
choices.C: It was neither inspected nor signed.
choices.D: It was inspected and not signed.

questions.correctAnswer: It was inspected and not signed.
questions.explanation: An unsealed form cannot be signed because signing requires sealing; acceptance then requires inspection as the other exclusive possibility.

questions.prompt: A taunt intended to GOAD someone into replying is intended to:
questions.explanation: Goad means provoke or urge into action; the taunt seeks a response rather than offering comfort, information, or protection.

questions.prompt: An obstacle that STYMIES an effort most nearly:
questions.explanation: Stymie means obstruct or frustrate progress; an obstacle that stymies an effort prevents it from advancing as intended.

questions.prompt: A STOLID observer is most nearly:
questions.explanation: Stolid describes an unemotional, impassive manner; restlessness, impulsiveness, and dramatic expression contrast with that steadiness.

questions.prompt: After resting, her movements were no longer LANGUID. Which description is most nearly opposite to LANGUID?
questions.explanation: Languid suggests low energy or sluggishness; vigorous indicates energetic, forceful movement rather than continued listlessness or ease.

questions.prompt: Which description is most nearly opposite to TRITE, describing a remark?

choices.C: familiar to the point of dullness

questions.explanation: Trite means unoriginal through overuse; a fresh, original remark contrasts with the familiar expressions described by the other choices.

questions.prompt: Which word is most nearly opposite to VORACIOUS, describing someone’s eating habits?
questions.explanation: Voracious describes consuming eagerly or in large amounts; abstemious describes restraint in eating and drinking, reversing that tendency.

questions.prompt: A partition divides existing space into separate rooms without adding floor area. Which change is most similar?

choices.A: A new page adds several new sentences.
choices.B: A translation replaces one language with another.
choices.C: A photocopy creates another complete document.
choices.D: A paragraph break divides existing text without adding words.

questions.correctAnswer: A paragraph break divides existing text without adding words.
questions.explanation: Both changes introduce an internal division while leaving the amount of underlying content unchanged; adding, translating, and duplicating perform different operations.

questions.prompt: A boat’s wake can mark its route after the boat has moved ahead. Which example has the most similar relationship?

choices.A: A contrail marks part of a plane’s route after the plane has passed.
choices.B: A weather vane shows the present wind direction.
choices.D: A beacon identifies its own fixed position.

questions.correctAnswer: A contrail marks part of a plane’s route after the plane has passed.
questions.explanation: The wake and contrail are lingering traces of an object’s past movement; the alternatives indicate a current direction or location.

questions.prompt: For a tenant, rent is an expense; for the owner, the SAME payment is income. Which case similarly names a SINGLE TRANSFER differently at its two ends?

choices.A: A box is empty at noon and full at dusk.
choices.B: A faded sign is repainted in a brighter color.
choices.C: A border crossing is a departure from one country and an arrival in the other.
choices.D: Two audiences give different ratings to a concert.

questions.correctAnswer: A border crossing is a departure from one country and an arrival in the other.
questions.explanation: Expense and income describe the same transferred payment from opposite sides, just as departure and arrival describe one crossing from its two endpoints.

questions.prompt: Which word belongs with KNEAD, WRING, and CLENCH because each can describe an action using hand pressure?
questions.explanation: Squeeze uses pressure from the hands, like kneading, wringing, or clenching; the other choices concern hearing, looking, or producing a sound.

questions.prompt: Which relationship, like IS NEXT TO, necessarily works in both directions?
questions.explanation: If one person is a sibling of another, the reverse relationship also holds; parenthood, greater age, and supervision do not reverse that way.

questions.prompt: Which group pairs each property with its denial, rather than merely with a different degree or an associated thing?
questions.explanation: Unequal, incomplete, and unoccupied deny the corresponding property; the other groups present degrees, roles with associated things, or related objects.

questions.prompt: A panel promises to CONSIDER every proposal. Later it rejects several after reviewing them. Which interpretation is consistent with the promise?

choices.A: Rejecting any proposal proves that it was never reviewed.
choices.B: Reviewing every proposal does not require approving every proposal.
choices.C: The promise guarantees approval of every proposal.
choices.D: Only proposals that are approved can be considered.

questions.correctAnswer: Reviewing every proposal does not require approving every proposal.
questions.explanation: Consideration is the review process, while approval is one possible outcome; rejecting a reviewed proposal does not violate the promise to consider it.

questions.prompt: A codebook defines ZEL as NAR and NAR as ZEL, giving no examples or other definitions. Why might this fail to teach a new reader either meaning?

choices.A: The two definitions prove that the terms are opposites.
choices.B: Definitions must always appear in reverse alphabetical order.
choices.C: A codebook cannot contain more than one unfamiliar term.
choices.D: Each unfamiliar term is explained only through the other unfamiliar term.

questions.correctAnswer: Each unfamiliar term is explained only through the other unfamiliar term.
questions.explanation: The definitions form a circle without an independent explanation or example, so a reader who knows neither term gains no starting meaning.

questions.prompt: Assume a statement must be either true or false, but not both. A card says only, "This statement is false." What follows when each truth assignment is checked?

choices.A: Neither assignment consistently fits the statement’s own claim.
choices.B: Calling it true makes the card’s claim consistent.
choices.C: Calling it false confirms its claim is false.
choices.D: Its truth depends only on the card’s color.

questions.correctAnswer: Neither assignment consistently fits the statement’s own claim.
questions.explanation: If true, its claim makes it false; if false, its claim makes it true. Neither assignment remains consistent under the stated rule.

questions.prompt: To DECRY a practice publicly is to:
questions.explanation: Decry means express strong public disapproval; neutral description, enthusiastic approval, and concealment do not communicate that condemnation.

questions.prompt: To ATTUNE a plan to local conditions is to:

choices.C: adjust it to fit those conditions

questions.correctAnswer: adjust it to fit those conditions
questions.explanation: Attune means bring into harmony or adjustment; fitting the plan to local conditions expresses that relationship rather than announcing, repeating, or rejecting.

questions.prompt: Her RUEFUL smile followed the realization that she had caused the delay. RUEFUL most nearly means:
questions.explanation: Rueful expresses regret, sometimes with a wry acceptance of one’s own mistake; the delay she caused supplies that regretful context.

questions.prompt: Which description is most nearly opposite to RAUCOUS, describing a crowd’s voices?
questions.explanation: Raucous describes harsh, unpleasant loudness; quiet, subdued voices reverse that quality rather than restating its force or noise.

questions.prompt: The investigation exposed SORDID dealings marked by dishonesty. Which word is most nearly opposite to SORDID here?
questions.explanation: Sordid here means morally disgraceful or dishonorable; honorable reverses that ethical description, while the other choices reinforce it.

questions.prompt: Which word is most nearly opposite to WILY, describing a person?
questions.explanation: Wily means skilled in deceptive tricks; guileless describes someone without such deceit, whereas cunning, crafty, and sly retain it.

questions.prompt: A ruler’s evenly spaced marks indicate equal intervals of LENGTH. Which example has the most similar relationship to TIME?

choices.A: A steady metronome’s beats mark equal time intervals.
choices.B: An alarm announces one selected moment.
choices.C: A clock’s case protects its mechanism.
choices.D: A calendar cover displays a picture.

questions.correctAnswer: A steady metronome’s beats mark equal time intervals.
questions.explanation: Ruler marks and steady beats divide their respective dimensions into equal intervals; a single alarm, protective case, or cover illustration does not.

questions.prompt: A dimmer allows intermediate brightness settings, while a simple ON/OFF switch offers separate states. Which pair makes the corresponding contrast?

choices.B: Two ladders have different numbers of rungs.
choices.C: Two switches have differently colored buttons.
choices.D: A ramp provides a continuous incline, while a staircase provides separate standing levels.

questions.correctAnswer: A ramp provides a continuous incline, while a staircase provides separate standing levels.
questions.explanation: The matched contrast is continuous adjustment versus distinct levels; merely changing slope, rung count, or color does not reproduce that difference.

questions.prompt: A room can keep the SAME number of people while some leave and others enter. Which example has the same underlying relationship?

choices.A: A locked box retains its contents because nobody opens it.
choices.B: A reservoir’s water level stays constant because incoming water replaces outgoing water.
choices.C: An empty bottle becomes full as water is added.
choices.D: A picture changes color as more paint is applied.

questions.correctAnswer: A reservoir’s water level stays constant because incoming water replaces outgoing water.
questions.explanation: An unchanged total can conceal replacement of individual contents; the room and reservoir illustrate this, unlike no replacement or a visibly changing total.

questions.prompt: Which word belongs with POCKET, DRAWER, and COMPARTMENT because it names a small storage space?
questions.explanation: A cubby is a small compartment used for storage; hinges, handles, and latches are fittings rather than spaces that hold contents.

questions.prompt: Which group contains ONLY words that can signal a contrast with, or concession to, a preceding statement?
questions.explanation: However, nevertheless, and nonetheless can introduce contrast or concession; the other groups primarily concern reasons, sequence, or location.

questions.prompt: Which group contains ONLY ways of joining material by adding a separate fastening material or object?
questions.explanation: Sewing adds thread, stapling adds staples, and gluing adds adhesive; the other groups reshape, remove, or rearrange material without that fastening addition.

questions.prompt: One route planner selects the route with the FEWEST CHANGES. Another selects the one with the SHORTEST TRAVEL TIME. They recommend different routes. Why need this be no contradiction?

choices.A: The fewest changes must always mean the shortest time.
choices.B: Only one planner can define its selection rule.
choices.C: Every route necessarily takes the same amount of time.
choices.D: They judge routes by different criteria.

questions.correctAnswer: They judge routes by different criteria.
questions.explanation: A route can minimize transfers without minimizing elapsed time; different stated criteria can therefore produce different recommendations without logical conflict.

questions.prompt: A forecast proves incorrect. Someone concludes that the forecaster must have deliberately lied. Which distinction is missing?

choices.A: Being wrong does not by itself establish knowingly saying something false.
choices.B: An incorrect prediction can never be compared with what happens.
choices.C: Every prediction must be true when it is spoken.
choices.D: A sincere prediction cannot turn out to be wrong.

questions.correctAnswer: Being wrong does not by itself establish knowingly saying something false.
questions.explanation: A mistaken prediction and intentional deception differ in what the speaker believed; the later error alone does not establish deliberate falsehood.

questions.prompt: A report concludes that ALL engineers prefer Tool Q after interviewing ONLY engineers who had already named Q as their favorite. Which criticism is strongest?

choices.A: Every engineer excluded from the interviews must dislike Q.
choices.B: The selection ensures favorable answers from those invited but does not establish everyone else’s preference.
choices.C: The conclusion must be false merely because some engineers were not interviewed.
choices.D: Engineers cannot have meaningful preferences about tools.

questions.correctAnswer: The selection ensures favorable answers from those invited but does not establish everyone else’s preference.
questions.explanation: Selecting known supporters makes their agreement unsurprising; it supplies no basis for extending the preference to engineers who were excluded.
